title.value: Generative lesion pattern decomposition of cognitive impairment after stroke
title.justification: The title concisely captures the primary focus of the paper, which is on understanding cognitive impairment after stroke through the decomposition of lesion patterns.
title.quote: Generative lesion pattern decomposition of cognitive impairment after stroke

analysis.description: This paper explores the generative lesion pattern decomposition to understand cognitive impairment post-stroke. The study uses machine learning and Bayesian hierarchical modeling to evaluate hemisphere-specific effects and predicts cognitive outcomes in stroke patients.

type.justification: The study involves data analysis of 1080 stroke patients, applying machine learning and Bayesian hierarchical models to predict cognitive outcomes, which is characteristic of empirical research.
type.quote: Therefore, in this proof-of-principle study, we sought to integrate machine learning and Bayesian hierarchical modelling to enable a hemisphere-aware analysis of 1080 ischaemic stroke patients.

name.justification: The focus on cognitive impairment post-stroke, and the methods used, place the paper within the neuroscience domain.
name.quote: Neuroimaging data pre-processing... Brain-imaging acquisition was typically performed within the first week after stroke.

name.justification: The paper applies neuroimaging and cognitive assessments to stroke patient data, emphasizing clinical applications.
name.quote: Cognitive impairment is a frequent and disabling sequela of stroke...

name.justification: The study involves the acquisition and analysis of brain imaging data from stroke patients.
name.quote: Neuroimaging data pre-processing... Brain-imaging acquisition was typically performed within the first week after stroke.

name.justification: NMF was used as a multivariate encoding strategy to identify lesion patterns.
name.quote: We then applied non-negative matrix factorization (NMF) as a multivariate encoding strategy to identify 10 unique combinations of spatially distributed region damage.

is_contributed.justification: NMF is used as a known technique within the study, not contributed by the paper.
